comments.author: @travellives
comments.text: If you grew up on Montserrat or have family there, what’s one detail of daily life you’d want someone overseas to understand? We’d love to hear a memory from your village or your family’s Friday table.

comments.author: @Jos_611
comments.text: I suppose Montserrat is shaped like Antigua now? 1:26. You really need to do better with your facts.  Also the May  1991 census showed the population to be 11,314. Montserrat has two 2 private primary schools, not 1 one. 😊Mistakes in most if not all of your videos😮

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: We truly appreciate you helping us keep our facts accurate, and we'll certainly double check these details in future videos. Thanks again for your support!

comments.author: @Linda-y3m7k
comments.text: Okay, I have to ask anyone from Montserrat who makes goat water at home… bread or rice on the side? 😄

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: Now that’s a question for a Montserratian cook. I suspect it depends on whose kitchen you’re in 😄

comments.author: @Mccormick-w8r
comments.text: I came for the story of the volcano, but I ended up wondering where everyone went to school once Plymouth was evacuated. Glad the film spent some time on that.

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: Glad that part stayed with you. Kids go to primary school in Brades and Lookout today. It’s a side of Montserrat we wanted to show.
